Navagraha Remedies: Mantras, Gemstones & Rituals for the 9 Planets

Traditional Navagraha remedies for each of the 9 planets — mantras, gemstones, colors and simple rituals used to pacify a difficult graha.

Key Takeaways

  • •Navagraha remedies are traditional practices — mantras, gemstones, colors, fasting and simple rituals — used in Jyotish to ease the effect of a weak or difficult planet in a birth chart.
  • •Each of the nine grahas has its own seed mantra, gemstone, color and day of the week traditionally associated with it.
  • •The most commonly recommended remedy across nearly every graha is chanting its mantra with consistency, since it requires no special equipment or expense.
  • •Remedies are a traditional, symbolic practice for reflection and reassurance — not a scientifically verified intervention, and never a substitute for real-world action or professional advice.
Parikshiva Published August 3, 2026 3 min read

On this page

  • Remedies for Each of the Nine Grahas
  • How to Actually Practice a Navagraha Remedy
  • Remedies During a Difficult Dasha

When a Jyotish reading identifies a weak, afflicted, or currently-active difficult graha in a birth chart, the tradition doesn't stop at diagnosis — it offers a set of traditional responses known as Navagraha remedies (Upayas). These range from a mantra chanted quietly at home to a formal temple ritual conducted by a priest, and every one of the nine grahas has its own specific set of traditional pairings: a mantra, a gemstone, a color, and a preferred day. This guide walks through the most common remedy for each graha, and is written specifically as the practical companion to our full guide to the Navagraha themselves.

Remedies for Each of the Nine Grahas

  • Surya (Sun) — Mantra: "Om Suryaya Namaha." Color: red or orange. Gemstone: ruby. Traditional day: Sunday. Simple ritual: offering water to the rising sun (Surya Arghya).
  • Chandra (Moon) — Mantra: "Om Chandraya Namaha." Color: white. Gemstone: pearl or moonstone. Traditional day: Monday. Simple ritual: fasting on Monday, or offering milk.
  • Mangal (Mars) — Mantra: "Om Mangalaya Namaha." Color: red. Gemstone: red coral. Traditional day: Tuesday. Simple ritual: donating red lentils or offering to Hanuman.
  • Budha (Mercury) — Mantra: "Om Budhaya Namaha." Color: green. Gemstone: emerald. Traditional day: Wednesday. Simple ritual: donating green vegetables or green cloth.
  • Guru (Jupiter) — Mantra: "Om Gurave Namaha." Color: yellow. Gemstone: yellow sapphire. Traditional day: Thursday. Simple ritual: respecting teachers and elders; donating yellow foods like turmeric or chickpeas.
  • Shukra (Venus) — Mantra: "Om Shukraya Namaha." Color: white or pastel shades. Gemstone: diamond or white sapphire. Traditional day: Friday. Simple ritual: offering white flowers, or acts of generosity toward women.
  • Shani (Saturn) — Mantra: "Om Shanaye Namaha." Color: dark blue or black. Gemstone: blue sapphire. Traditional day: Saturday. Simple ritual: donating black sesame seeds or serving the underprivileged.
  • Rahu — Mantra: "Om Rahave Namaha." Color: smoky grey or brown. Gemstone: hessonite (gomed). Traditional day: often paired with Saturday. Simple ritual: charity toward the marginalized; avoiding shortcuts or deception in daily conduct.
  • Ketu — Mantra: "Om Ketave Namaha." Color: grey. Gemstone: cat's eye (lehsunia). Traditional day: often paired with Tuesday. Simple ritual: quiet meditation and simplicity; donating sesame or blankets to those in need.

How to Actually Practice a Navagraha Remedy

The single most accessible remedy, across nearly every graha, is simply chanting that graha's mantra with consistency — no gemstone, temple visit, or priest required. Most traditional guidance recommends repeating the mantra 108 times, using a mala (a string of prayer beads) to keep count without breaking focus, ideally on that graha's ruling day of the week or during its ruling planetary hour. A gemstone or specific color is treated as a complementary layer on top of this — never a replacement for the core mantra practice, and never something to buy or wear without first understanding what it is meant to support.

Start with the mantra, not the gemstone

Traditional Jyotish is clear that a gemstone worn without the corresponding mantra practice, or worn for the wrong graha for your specific chart, is not considered a meaningful remedy on its own. If you are new to this, start with the mantra and a consistent day of practice before considering any gemstone purchase — and ideally consult an experienced Jyotish practitioner about your specific chart first.

Remedies During a Difficult Dasha

Remedies are most often sought during a Dasha (planetary period) ruled by a graha that sits weak or afflicted in the birth chart — a Saturn Dasha for someone with a difficult Saturn, for instance. The remedy doesn't claim to erase the period's themes entirely; the traditional framing is closer to a support that helps a person move through a challenging period with more steadiness and awareness, rather than a way to skip past it.

A remedy is not a shortcut around a difficult period — it is a way of meeting it with steadier hands.

A traditional practice, not a guaranteed outcome

Navagraha remedies are a traditional, symbolic practice within Jyotish, offered here for cultural and educational understanding. They are not scientifically verified, do not guarantee any specific outcome, and should never replace real-world action, financial planning, or professional medical or legal advice where those are genuinely needed.
